tier_reason: The project's own README table lists dictionary sizes for 9,805,576 English Wikipedia titles (enwiki-20121101, 200,435,403 bytes plain): darts-clone 376,613,888 bytes, tx-trie 127,727,058, marisa-trie 50,753,560. There is no harness, compiler, flags or hardware for that table, and tools/marisa-benchmark.cc includes only marisa.h (no darts-clone or tx-trie comparison), so the tier is C.

corrections.caveats: The README table reports size only, with no speed numbers, compiler or hardware, and the measurement dates from 2012-era data. The repo's tools/marisa-benchmark.cc times marisa alone (build, lookup, reverse lookup, prefix and predictive search) and does not run darts-clone or tx-trie. darts-clone is already catalogued in this wave, so this is a size-only win over it: The page gives no lookup-speed comparison, so speed against darts-clone is unverified. Recent commits are mostly dependabot CI bumps; the last maintainer commit was 2026-02-11. The readthedocs benchmark page for the Python bindings was not opened (readthedocs blocked).

notes: The size numbers and ratios in claimed_speedup match the README (2.5x vs tx-trie, 7.4x vs darts-clone, derived from page data). Metadata confirmed from the github.com page: 633 stars, 103 forks, not archived, not a fork, BSD-2-Clause OR LGPL-2.1-or-later (COPYING.md), last commit 2026-07-28 (dependabot), so active. Treat this as a memory/size entry, not a speed entry.
